full_judgment: 83. In Government Appeal No.5 of 1992, we find that the trial Court considered the evidence of PWs 38 and 45 read with exhibits 9/100, 58-62 and material exhibits XIV-XIV/30 and assigned sufficient reasons in acquitting the accused-respondent (appellant in the criminal appeal) of charge under section 5(2) of the Act II of 1947 allegedly for commission of offence under section 5(1) (c) thereof. On sifting the evidence regarding this part of the charges, we also do not find anything wrong in the order of acquittal. This part of the occurrences allegedly took place when the appellant possessed the office of President, but still the trial so far it relates to the charge under the said provision was illegal for misjoinder of charges triable under two different special laws by two different Tribunals. When the trial itself was illegal for misjoinder of charges, the question of enhancement of sentence or awarding that under section 5(2) for commission of offence under section 5(1) (c) of the Act on setting aside the acquittal does not arise. We thus do not find any merit in Government Appeal No.5 of 1992.
